panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Chest CT panel from a glanders case report showing hilar lymphadenomegaly and segmental compressive atelectasis; these specific findings are not in the provided vocabulary, but the panel is a real patient image from the glanders case and supports pulmonary involvement. B: Axial chest CT from a confirmed glanders case showing bilateral pleural effusion, a recognized glanders manifestation, with basal consolidations and pericardial effusion; caption and in-text support pleural effusion/pneumonia in the patient. C: Chest CT from a glanders case showing peripheral nodular opacities and subpleural consolidations; no exact matching vocabulary term, but the panel is a real patient image supporting pulmonary glanders. D: Chest CT from a glanders case showing bilateral ground-glass opacities and consolidations due to pulmonary inflammation; no exact vocabulary term, but real patient image from the glanders case.

plate_findings.evidence: Caption: 'Coronal section, showing a heterogeneous pattern of lung attenuation' in a patient infected with Burkholderia mallei

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Coronal contrast chest CT of a PCR-confirmed human B. mallei (glanders) case showing heterogeneous pulmonary attenuation, a recognized pulmonary manifestation of acute glanders. B: Axial chest CT from the same PCR-confirmed glanders patient showing consolidative opacities and subsegmental atelectasis, consistent with pulmonary glanders.
panels.attribution_text: Luz et al. Clinical and Molecular Characterization of Human Burkholderia mallei Infection, Brazil.. Emerging infectious diseases 2024. doi:10.3201/eid3011.240549. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 1.
panels.figure_caption: Computed tomography with contrast of the chest of a patient from Brazil infected with Burkholderia mallei. A) Coronal section, showing a heterogeneous pattern of lung attenuation. Arrows marked 1 indicate a suggestive disturbance in the ventilation-perfusion relationship. B) Axial section. Arrow marked 2 indicates consolidative opacities. Arrows marked 3 indicate subsegmental atelectasis in both lungs.
in_text_mentions: a glanders-positive horse at a vaquejada training center. In the Northeast Region, equestrian events bring together horses from various sources, which increases the risk for B. mallei transmission and infection. Close interactions between horse owners and horses raise the likelihood of human exposure to infected animals. After 6 days of hospitalization, the patient underwent a computed tomography of his chest (Figure 1). On day 7 of hospitalization, a 25-mL sample of pleural drainage was collected and transported to the Embrapa Beef Cattle Biosafety Level 3 laboratory in Campo Grande, Brazil.

PCR amplifications targeting B. mallei loci (Appendix Table 1) from pleural drainage and bacterial isolate DNA yielded positive results. In addition, Burk475 PCR, which is designed to detect both B. mallei and B. pseudomallei, demonstrated positive amplification. The PCR targeting the open reading frame 11 marker for B. pseudomallei was negative (Figures 1, 2; Appendix). The amplicon sequencing results (Appendix Table 2) confirmed exact matches with B. mallei from PCR targeting the species.
